# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write

- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T21:42:52Z

## PR Description

Closes #1065
### Root Cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` and each event started its own run — one human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM `workflow_dispatch` path only; the GitHub-event path bypassed it (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs, owner hand-cancelling duplicates). The per-issue `concurrency:` group only serialized the duplicates into queued no-op burns — it never dropped them.

### Fix

- `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (new): the unit-tested pure decision, gh-1028 parity — same issue + same leg (title-parsed; unknown leg wildcards on either side, known legs must be equal), in-flight (active states, 6h stale-zombie bound) or freshly-completed `success` (10-min freshness window — burst duplicates reach the probe only after the concurrency group releases the first run) ⇒ skip. Strict run_number tie-break: only an OLDER run suppresses, so exactly one survivor per same-second burst. Fail-open on missing/garbled run data (AC3).
- `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`: new `dedup` probe job (per-status `gh api` fan-out, smAgent parity; short-circuits before any API call for `workflow_dispatch`, non-arming lifecycle labels, non-teammate assignees — gh-1029 no-burn parity; catch-all probe-error fail-open). The `teammate` call now gates on `needs: dedup.outputs.proceed == 'true'`; dropped duplicates emit a `::warning::` audit line (AC1). Dispatch-path behaviour unchanged.
- `js/unit-tests/test_teammateEventDedup.js` + `run_teammateEventDedup.json` (new), added to `run_all.json`.

### Test Coverage

- `test_teammateEventDedup.js` — 30 tests, incl. AC4 (simulated assigned+labeled burst → exactly one dispatch + one skip-audit entry; three-event gh-1061 shape), AC2 (fresh-success suppression after concurrency release; known different leg never swallowed; 6h zombie parity), AC3 (broken/missing probe data proceeds). **PASS**
- Workflow wiring guard: dedup job, `needs.dedup` gate, fail-open anchors asserted against the YAML. **PASS**
- Transport smoke: embedded probe script executed against a mocked `gh` — duplicate drop, earliest-proceeds tie-break, 5/5-status-degraded fail-open, dispatch preflight all verified.
- Full suite `run_all.json`: **4548 passed, 0 failed** (was 4548-green baseline + 30 new).

### Notes

- Freshness window is 10 min by design (documented in the module): long enough for burst event delivery + queue lag, short enough that a later human re-assign is never swallowed. Only `conclusion: success` owns the window — cancelled/failed runs leave the retry path open.
- `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (consumer-repo copy) not touched — its run titles already carry the leg; a follow-up can mirror the gate there if wanted.
- The probe adds one small job per arming event (~seconds: checkout + ≤5 API calls); lifecycle-label events short-circuit with zero API calls.

# pr-1071: gh-1065 [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)

## Description

Closes #1065
### Root Cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` and each event started its own run — one human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM `workflow_dispatch` path only; the GitHub-event path bypassed it (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs, owner hand-cancelling duplicates). The per-issue `concurrency:` group only serialized the duplicates into queued no-op burns — it never dropped them.

### Fix

- `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (new): the unit-tested pure decision, gh-1028 parity — same issue + same leg (title-parsed; unknown leg wildcards on either side, known legs must be equal), in-flight (active states, 6h stale-zombie bound) or freshly-completed `success` (10-min freshness window — burst duplicates reach the probe only after the concurrency group releases the first run) ⇒ skip. Strict run_number tie-break: only an OLDER run suppresses, so exactly one survivor per same-second burst. Fail-open on missing/garbled run data (AC3).
- `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`: new `dedup` probe job (per-status `gh api` fan-out, smAgent parity; short-circuits before any API call for `workflow_dispatch`, non-arming lifecycle labels, non-teammate assignees — gh-1029 no-burn parity; catch-all probe-error fail-open). The `teammate` call now gates on `needs: dedup.outputs.proceed == 'true'`; dropped duplicates emit a `::warning::` audit line (AC1). Dispatch-path behaviour unchanged.
- `js/unit-tests/test_teammateEventDedup.js` + `run_teammateEventDedup.json` (new), added to `run_all.json`.

### Test Coverage

- `test_teammateEventDedup.js` — 30 tests, incl. AC4 (simulated assigned+labeled burst → exactly one dispatch + one skip-audit entry; three-event gh-1061 shape), AC2 (fresh-success suppression after concurrency release; known different leg never swallowed; 6h zombie parity), AC3 (broken/missing probe data proceeds). **PASS**
- Workflow wiring guard: dedup job, `needs.dedup` gate, fail-open anchors asserted against the YAML. **PASS**
- Transport smoke: embedded probe script executed against a mocked `gh` — duplicate drop, earliest-proceeds tie-break, 5/5-status-degraded fail-open, dispatch preflight all verified.
- Full suite `run_all.json`: **4548 passed, 0 failed** (was 4548-green baseline + 30 new).

### Notes

- Freshness window is 10 min by design (documented in the module): long enough for burst event delivery + queue lag, short enough that a later human re-assign is never swallowed. Only `conclusion: success` owns the window — cancelled/failed runs leave the retry path open.
- `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (consumer-repo copy) not touched — its run titles already carry the leg; a follow-up can mirror the gate there if wanted.
- The probe adds one small job per arming event (~seconds: checkout + ≤5 API calls); lifecycle-label events short-circuit with zero API calls.

`quality.yml` sets `CRAP_THRESHOLD: 8` and fails when *a function not in the released baseline exceeds the threshold*. All four functions are new, so none is baselined. Since CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)³ + CC, the best possible value (100% coverage) is CRAP = CC — so `decideEventDedup` scores **≥ 27** no matter how well the 30 tests cover it. The gate cannot go green without refactoring.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` line 212

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: runs that never executed the teammate leg own the freshness window — the first GENUINE trigger is silently swallowed**

`isFreshlyCompleted` (and the transport around it) treats any `status: completed` + `conclusion: success` run of this workflow as an owner of the issue+leg key. But run-level success no longer implies the leg ran, because the new `dedup` job **always executes and always succeeds** (its catch-all is fail-open by design):

- A non-arming lifecycle label write (`status:*`, `ai_developed`, … — which the legs themselves write constantly, see the gh-1029 comment in the workflow) creates a run whose `teammate` job is skipped by the gate. The `dedup` job succeeds → **the run concludes `success`**, titled `teammate: issues #1040 ` (same issue anchor, leg `''` → wildcard-compatible).
- Now a human assigns the issue to `ai-teammate (or adds `agent:review`) within 10 minutes of that label write. The probe finds this fresh `success` run, older run_number → `duplicate` → **the first and only real trigger is dropped**, with nothing but a `::warning::` line inside a run that GitHub shows as green.

This breaks AC1 in the dangerous direction (zero runs instead of one), and it contradicts AC3's spirit — a dedup check silently swallowing the only trigger. During active work on an issue (labels being written by legs), event-path triggers are effectively suppressed for 10 minutes after ANY run of this workflow, successful or not.

Suggested directions (either or both):
1. Before a `completed` candidate may suppress, verify it actually executed the leg: `gh api repos/{repo}/actions/runs/{id}/jobs` and require a non-`dedup` job with conclusion `success`. One extra API call only when a candidate exists; keeps the module pure via an injected transport hook.
2. Give the `dedup` job an `if:` mirroring the arming gate (see the runner-burn comment on the workflow) so non-arming events produce zero executed jobs — those runs then conclude `failure` (the gh-676 phantom pattern) and own nothing.

Note the unit suite cannot catch this today: the tests feed synthetic run lists where `conclusion: 'success'` is assumed to mean "the leg ran". A regression test needs the transport-level distinction from option 1, or the zero-job conclusion from option 2.

---

### Thread 3 — `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` line 80

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the unguarded `dedup` job allocates a runner for EVERY label write — gh-1029 no-burn regression**

The `dedup` job has no `if:`, and `on: issues: types: [assigned, labeled]` fires on every label write on every issue — including the lifecycle-label storms the legs themselves generate (`status:*`, `ai_developed`, …). gh-1029 deliberately made those events no-burn: the run's only job was skipped by the gate, zero jobs executed, no runner allocated. This PR keeps the skip but adds a real `ubuntu-latest` runner + checkout + node boot (~30–60 s of runner time) per label write, repo-wide, around the clock.

The preflight correctly avoids *API* calls for non-arming events, but the runner burn remains. Please add an `if:` to the `dedup` job mirroring the `teammate` gate (dispatch OR (assigned AND ai-teammate assignee) OR labeled with an arming label). Behaviour is unchanged for admitted events; rejected events return to true zero-burn.

Side benefit relevant to the freshness-window blocker on `isFreshlyCompleted`: with the `dedup` job skipped, those runs execute zero jobs and conclude `failure` (the gh-676 phantom pattern documented in this same file) — so they stop owning the dedup key entirely.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the wildcard leg + 10-min fresh-success window swallows genuinely sequential human actions**

`legsCompatible` wildcards an unknown leg on either side — correct for the in-flight burst (event-path titles carry no leg, and a bare assign declares none). But the same wildcard is applied to `completed` runs inside the freshness window, where the owner is an event-path run titled `teammate: issues #1040 ` (leg `''`).

Consequence: human assigns the issue at T (leg runs, completes `success` at T+4 min). At T+6 min the same human deliberately adds `agent:review` — a genuinely new request, not a burst duplicate. The probe sees the T+4 `success` run: same issue, leg wildcard-compatible, older run_number → **dropped**. The module docstring claims "a later human re-assign is never swallowed", but that only holds after the 10-minute window; any second, *different-leg* arming action within the window is swallowed.

Please confirm this is intended (the PR notes treat the 10-min bound as covering "burst event delivery + queue lag", i.e. seconds — while a human's next deliberate action often lands minutes later, within the same active session). If not intended, consider scoping the wildcard to in-flight owners only: a wildcard **in-flight** owner is almost certainly the same burst; a `completed` owner with unknown leg suppressing a KNOWN new leg is exactly the sequential-action case. At minimum, the docstring's "never swallowed" claim should be corrected.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1071
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1071
- **Title**: gh-1065 [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1065` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +924
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:30:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T21:42:52Z

## PR Description

Closes #1065
### Root Cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` and each event started its own run — one human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM `workflow_dispatch` path only; the GitHub-event path bypassed it (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs, owner hand-cancelling duplicates). The per-issue `concurrency:` group only serialized the duplicates into queued no-op burns — it never dropped them.

### Fix

- `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (new): the unit-tested pure decision, gh-1028 parity — same issue + same leg (title-parsed; unknown leg wildcards on either side, known legs must be equal), in-flight (active states, 6h stale-zombie bound) or freshly-completed `success` (10-min freshness window — burst duplicates reach the probe only after the concurrency group releases the first run) ⇒ skip. Strict run_number tie-break: only an OLDER run suppresses, so exactly one survivor per same-second burst. Fail-open on missing/garbled run data (AC3).
- `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`: new `dedup` probe job (per-status `gh api` fan-out, smAgent parity; short-circuits before any API call for `workflow_dispatch`, non-arming lifecycle labels, non-teammate assignees — gh-1029 no-burn parity; catch-all probe-error fail-open). The `teammate` call now gates on `needs: dedup.outputs.proceed == 'true'`; dropped duplicates emit a `::warning::` audit line (AC1). Dispatch-path behaviour unchanged.
- `js/unit-tests/test_teammateEventDedup.js` + `run_teammateEventDedup.json` (new), added to `run_all.json`.

### Test Coverage

- `test_teammateEventDedup.js` — 30 tests, incl. AC4 (simulated assigned+labeled burst → exactly one dispatch + one skip-audit entry; three-event gh-1061 shape), AC2 (fresh-success suppression after concurrency release; known different leg never swallowed; 6h zombie parity), AC3 (broken/missing probe data proceeds). **PASS**

# pr-1071: gh-1065 [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)

## Description

Closes #1065
### Root Cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` and each event started its own run — one human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM `workflow_dispatch` path only; the GitHub-event path bypassed it (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs, owner hand-cancelling duplicates). The per-issue `concurrency:` group only serialized the duplicates into queued no-op burns — it never dropped them.

### Fix

- `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (new): the unit-tested pure decision, gh-1028 parity — same issue + same leg (title-parsed; unknown leg wildcards on either side, known legs must be equal), in-flight (active states, 6h stale-zombie bound) or freshly-completed `success` (10-min freshness window — burst duplicates reach the probe only after the concurrency group releases the first run) ⇒ skip. Strict run_number tie-break: only an OLDER run suppresses, so exactly one survivor per same-second burst. Fail-open on missing/garbled run data (AC3).
- `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`: new `dedup` probe job (per-status `gh api` fan-out, smAgent parity; short-circuits before any API call for `workflow_dispatch`, non-arming lifecycle labels, non-teammate assignees — gh-1029 no-burn parity; catch-all probe-error fail-open). The `teammate` call now gates on `needs: dedup.outputs.proceed == 'true'`; dropped duplicates emit a `::warning::` audit line (AC1). Dispatch-path behaviour unchanged.
- `js/unit-tests/test_teammateEventDedup.js` + `run_teammateEventDedup.json` (new), added to `run_all.json`.

AC4 (simulated assigned+labeled burst → exactly one dispatch + one skip-audit entry; three-event gh-1061 shape), AC2 (fresh-success suppression after concurrency release; known different leg never swallowed; 6h zombie parity), AC3 (broken/missing probe data proceeds). **PASS**

- Transport smoke: embedded probe script executed against a mocked `gh` — duplicate drop, earliest-proceeds tie-break, 5/5-status-degraded fail-open, dispatch preflight all verified.

### Notes

- Freshness window is 10 min by design (documented in the module): long enough for burst event delivery + queue lag, short enough that a later human re-assign is never swallowed. Only `conclusion: success` owns the window — cancelled/failed runs leave the retry path open.

### Thread 2 — `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` line 212

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: runs that never executed the teammate leg own the freshness window — the first GENUINE trigger is silently swallowed**

`isFreshlyCompleted` (and the transport around it) treats any `status: completed` + `conclusion: success` run of this workflow as an owner of the issue+leg key. But run-level success no longer implies the leg ran, because the new `dedup` job **always executes and always succeeds** (its catch-all is fail-open by design):

The `dedup` job succeeds → **the run concludes `success`**, titled `teammate: issues #1040 ` (same issue anchor, leg `''` → wildcard-compatible).

The probe finds this fresh `success` run, older run_number → `duplicate` → **the first and only real trigger is dropped**, with nothing but a `::warning::` line inside a run that GitHub shows as green.

This breaks AC1 in the dangerous direction (zero runs instead of one), and it contradicts AC3's spirit — a dedup check silently swallowing the only trigger. During active work on an issue (labels being written by legs), event-path triggers are effectively suppressed for 10 minutes after ANY run of this workflow, successful or not.

Suggested directions (either or both):
1. Before a `completed` candidate may suppress, verify it actually executed the leg: `gh api repos/{repo}/actions/runs/{id}/jobs` and require a non-`dedup` job with conclusion `success`. One extra API call only when a candidate exists; keeps the module pure via an injected transport hook.
2. Give the `dedup` job an `if:` mirroring the arming gate (see the runner-burn comment on the workflow) so non-arming events produce zero executed jobs — those runs then conclude `failure` (the gh-676 phantom pattern) and own nothing.

Note the unit suite cannot catch this today: the tests feed synthetic run lists where `conclusion: 'success'` is assumed to mean "the leg ran". A regression test needs the transport-level distinction from option 1, or the zero-job conclusion from option 2.

---

### Thread 3 — `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` line 80

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the unguarded `dedup` job allocates a runner for EVERY label write — gh-1029 no-burn regression**

The `dedup` job has no `if:`, and `on: issues: types: [assigned, labeled]` fires on every label write on every issue — including the lifecycle-label storms the legs themselves generate (`status:*`, `ai_developed`, …). gh-1029 deliberately made those events no-burn: the run's only job was skipped by the gate, zero jobs executed, no runner allocated. This PR keeps the skip but adds a real `ubuntu-latest` runner + checkout + node boot (~30–60 s of runner time) per label write, repo-wide, around the clock.

The preflight correctly avoids *API* calls for non-arming events, but the runner burn remains. Please add an `if:` to the `dedup` job mirroring the `teammate` gate (dispatch OR (assigned AND ai-teammate assignee) OR labeled with an arming label). Behaviour is unchanged for admitted events; rejected events return to true zero-burn.

Side benefit relevant to the freshness-window blocker on `isFreshlyCompleted`: with the `dedup` job skipped, those runs execute zero jobs and conclude `failure` (the gh-676 phantom pattern documented in this same file) — so they stop owning the dedup key entirely.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the wildcard leg + 10-min fresh-success window swallows genuinely sequential human actions**

`legsCompatible` wildcards an unknown leg on either side — correct for the in-flight burst (event-path titles carry no leg, and a bare assign declares none). But the same wildcard is applied to `completed` runs inside the freshness window, where the owner is an event-path run titled `teammate: issues #1040 ` (leg `''`).

Consequence: human assigns the issue at T (leg runs, completes `success` at T+4 min). At T+6 min the same human deliberately adds `agent:review` — a genuinely new request, not a burst duplicate. The probe sees the T+4 `success` run: same issue, leg wildcard-compatible, older run_number → **dropped**. The module docstring claims "a later human re-assign is never swallowed", but that only holds after the 10-minute window; any second, *different-leg* arming action within the window is swallowed.

Please confirm this is intended (the PR notes treat the 10-min bound as covering "burst event delivery + queue lag", i.e. seconds — while a human's next deliberate action often lands minutes later, within the same active session). If not intended, consider scoping the wildcard to in-flight owners only: a wildcard **in-flight** owner is almost certainly the same burst; a `completed` owner with unknown leg suppressing a KNOWN new leg is exactly the sequential-action case. At minimum, the docstring's "never swallowed" claim should be corrected.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi

**Thread 2 (BLOCKING — skipped-leg runs own freshness window)**: Two suggested fixes. Best combined approach:
- Add `if:` to dedup job (thread 3) so non-arming events produce zero jobs → runs conclude failure → own nothing. This is the simplest and addresses both threads 2 & 3 partially.

With the `if:` on dedup, non-arming events → dedup skipped → run has zero jobs → conclusion failure. But what about arming events where teammate is skipped due to dedup gate (duplicate)? Those runs: dedup succeeds (proceed=false), teammate skipped → run concludes success. Hmm — but that's fine because that run DID represent the same leg trigger being processed... wait, no. A duplicate run that dropped its trigger concludes success with title `teammate: issues #1040 `. If a subsequent genuinely new trigger arrives within 10 min, the fresh-success duplicate owner would swallow it. Is that wrong? The duplicate run is a duplicate of the same human action — the first run is still in flight or recently completed. Actually if run A (proceeds, runs the leg) and run B (duplicate, skipped teammate, dedup success) both conclude... run B concludes success quickly. Run A may still be in flight or complete. A third event within 10 minutes would be suppressed by A anyway (in flight or fresh success). So the duplicate's success is mostly redundant with A's ownership. The dangerous case the reviewer flagged: non-arming lifecycle label write → dedup runs, proceeds=true (preflight), teammate skipped by its gate, run concludes success → owns the window for an issue that never had a leg run. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write

Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. — must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([All findings fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["PR Rework TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it"] R2["✅ If the existing tests only cover a single-item/simple case, add a test for the multi-item/edge case the finding points at — a fix without a test for that exact case is not verified"] R3["✅ Returned findings: your fix must differ from the previous attempt and the new/updated test must prove it"] R4["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] R5["✅ Verification order: finalize ALL fixes BEFORE launching the full test-suite/coverage run — a run over a tree you are still editing is wasted"] R6["✅ Long runs (full suite, coverage) start with bash background: true and are collected via bash_job status/output between other steps — NEVER foreground sleep-polling (see prompts/bash_tools.md)"] R7["❌ NEVER kill a running verification because files changed after it started — let it finish, treat the result as stale, re-run deliberately"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/response.md must be Markdown (# headings, - bullets, ``` code fences)"] F2["Required sections: ## Issues/Notes (if any), ## Approach, ## Files Modified, ## Test Coverage"] F3["Be surgical but thorough — fix exact issues flagged, then check …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1071
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1071
- **Title**: gh-1065 [GOAL] Dedup ai-teammate event triggers: assigning an issue starts duplicate teammate runs (assigned + labeled + SM dispatch race)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1065` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +924
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T21:30:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T21:42:52Z

## PR Description

Closes #1065
### Root Cause

`ai-teammate.yml` triggers on `issues: [assigned, labeled]` and each event started its own run — one human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits multiple events. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM `workflow_dispatch` path only; the GitHub-event path bypassed it (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061 three runs, owner hand-cancelling duplicates). The per-issue `concurrency:` group only serialized the duplicates into queued no-op burns — it never dropped them.

### Fix

- `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` (new): the unit-tested pure decision, gh-1028 parity — same issue + same leg (title-parsed; unknown leg wildcards on either side, known legs must be equal), in-flight (active states, 6h stale-zombie bound) or freshly-completed `success` (10-min freshness window — burst duplicates reach the probe only after the concurrency group releases the first run) ⇒ skip. Strict run_number tie-break: only an OLDER run suppresses, so exactly one survivor per same-second burst. Fail-open on missing/garbled run data (AC3).
- `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`: new `dedup` probe job (per-status `gh api` fan-out, smAgent parity; short-circuits before any API call for `workflow_dispatch`, non-arming lifecycle labels, non-teammate assignees — gh-1029 no-burn parity; catch-all probe-error fail-open). The `teammate` call now gates on `needs: dedup.outputs.proceed == 'true'`; dropped duplicates emit a `::warning::` audit line (AC1). Dispatch-path behaviour unchanged.
- `js/unit-tests/test_teammateEventDedup.js` + `run_teammateEventDedup.json` (new), added to `run_all.json`.

### Test Coverage

- `test_teammateEventDedup.js` — 30 tests, incl. AC4 (simulated assigned+labeled burst → exactly one dispatch + one skip-audit entry; three-event gh-1061 shape), AC2 (fresh-success suppression after concurrency release; known different leg never swallowed; 6h zombie parity), AC3 (broken/missing probe data proceeds). **PASS**
- Workflow wiring guard: dedup job, `needs.dedup` gate, fail-open anchors asserted against the YAML. **PASS**
- Transport smoke: embedded probe script executed against a mocked `gh` — duplicate drop, earliest-proceeds tie-break, 5/5-status-degraded fail-open, dispatch preflight all verified.
- Full suite `run_all.json`: **4548 passed, 0 failed** (was 4548-green baseline + 30 new).

### Notes

- Freshness window is 10 min by design (documented in the module): long enough for burst event delivery + queue lag, short enough that a later human re-assign is never swallowed. Only `conclusion: success` owns the window — cancelled/failed runs leave the retry path open.
- `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (consumer-repo copy) not touched — its run titles already carry the leg; a follow-up can mirror the gate there if wanted.
- The probe adds one small job per arming event (~seconds: checkout + ≤5 API calls); lifecycle-label events short-circuit with zero API calls.

# PR Discussion History

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` line 306

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `decideEventDedup` cannot pass the `crap` quality gate (CI is red)**

The `crap` check failed on this PR (log fetch was unavailable, but I reproduced the measurement locally with the workflow's exact pinned tool, `IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d` from `.github/workflows/quality.yml:26-27`):

```text
decideEventDedup   js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 27
issueOfRunName     js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 11
legOfRunName       js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 9
isOlderRun         js/common/teammateEventDedup.js   CC 9
```

`quality.yml` sets `CRAP_THRESHOLD: 8` and fails when *a function not in the released baseline exceeds the threshold*. All four functions are new, so none is baselined. Since CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)³ + CC, the best possible value (100% coverage) is CRAP = CC — so `decideEventDedup` scores **≥ 27** no matter how well the 30 tests cover it. The gate cannot go green without refactoring.

Please decompose `decideEventDedup` (e.g. extract the per-run suppressor predicate into a named helper — the six-condition loop body — and split the early-return verdict builders), and simplify `issueOfRunName`/`legOfRunName` (the two regex families could share one anchored-token scanner). Re-run `crap4js --threshold 8 js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` to confirm before pushing.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` line 212

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: runs that never executed the teammate leg own the freshness window — the first GENUINE trigger is silently swallowed**

`isFreshlyCompleted` (and the transport around it) treats any `status: completed` + `conclusion: success` run of this workflow as an owner of the issue+leg key. But run-level success no longer implies the leg ran, because the new `dedup` job **always executes and always succeeds** (its catch-all is fail-open by design):

- A non-arming lifecycle label write (`status:*`, `ai_developed`, … — which the legs themselves write constantly, see the gh-1029 comment in the workflow) creates a run whose `teammate` job is skipped by the gate. The `dedup` job succeeds → **the run concludes `success`**, titled `teammate: issues #1040 ` (same issue anchor, leg `''` → wildcard-compatible).
- Now a human assigns the issue to `ai-teammate (or adds `agent:review`) within 10 minutes of that label write. The probe finds this fresh `success` run, older run_number → `duplicate` → **the first and only real trigger is dropped**, with nothing but a `::warning::` line inside a run that GitHub shows as green.

This breaks AC1 in the dangerous direction (zero runs instead of one), and it contradicts AC3's spirit — a dedup check silently swallowing the only trigger. During active work on an issue (labels being written by legs), event-path triggers are effectively suppressed for 10 minutes after ANY run of this workflow, successful or not.

Suggested directions (either or both):
1. Before a `completed` candidate may suppress, verify it actually executed the leg: `gh api repos/{repo}/actions/runs/{id}/jobs` and require a non-`dedup` job with conclusion `success`. One extra API call only when a candidate exists; keeps the module pure via an injected transport hook.
2. Give the `dedup` job an `if:` mirroring the arming gate (see the runner-burn comment on the workflow) so non-arming events produce zero executed jobs — those runs then conclude `failure` (the gh-676 phantom pattern) and own nothing.

Note the unit suite cannot catch this today: the tests feed synthetic run lists where `conclusion: 'success'` is assumed to mean "the leg ran". A regression test needs the transport-level distinction from option 1, or the zero-job conclusion from option 2.

---

### Thread 3 — `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` line 80

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the unguarded `dedup` job allocates a runner for EVERY label write — gh-1029 no-burn regression**

The `dedup` job has no `if:`, and `on: issues: types: [assigned, labeled]` fires on every label write on every issue — including the lifecycle-label storms the legs themselves generate (`status:*`, `ai_developed`, …). gh-1029 deliberately made those events no-burn: the run's only job was skipped by the gate, zero jobs executed, no runner allocated. This PR keeps the skip but adds a real `ubuntu-latest` runner + checkout + node boot (~30–60 s of runner time) per label write, repo-wide, around the clock.

The preflight correctly avoids *API* calls for non-arming events, but the runner burn remains. Please add an `if:` to the `dedup` job mirroring the `teammate` gate (dispatch OR (assigned AND ai-teammate assignee) OR labeled with an arming label). Behaviour is unchanged for admitted events; rejected events return to true zero-burn.

Side benefit relevant to the freshness-window blocker on `isFreshlyCompleted`: with the `dedup` job skipped, those runs execute zero jobs and conclude `failure` (the gh-676 phantom pattern documented in this same file) — so they stop owning the dedup key entirely.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/common/teammateEventDedup.js` line 181

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the wildcard leg + 10-min fresh-success window swallows genuinely sequential human actions**

`legsCompatible` wildcards an unknown leg on either side — correct for the in-flight burst (event-path titles carry no leg, and a bare assign declares none). But the same wildcard is applied to `completed` runs inside the freshness window, where the owner is an event-path run titled `teammate: issues #1040 ` (leg `''`).

Consequence: human assigns the issue at T (leg runs, completes `success` at T+4 min). At T+6 min the same human deliberately adds `agent:review` — a genuinely new request, not a burst duplicate. The probe sees the T+4 `success` run: same issue, leg wildcard-compatible, older run_number → **dropped**. The module docstring claims "a later human re-assign is never swallowed", but that only holds after the 10-minute window; any second, *different-leg* arming action within the window is swallowed.

Please confirm this is intended (the PR notes treat the 10-min bound as covering "burst event delivery + queue lag", i.e. seconds — while a human's next deliberate action often lands minutes later, within the same active session). If not intended, consider scoping the wildcard to in-flight owners only: a wildcard **in-flight** owner is almost certainly the same burst; a `completed` owner with unknown leg suppressing a KNOWN new leg is exactly the sequential-action case. At minimum, the docstring's "never swallowed" claim should be corrected.

---

### Thread 5 — `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` line 96

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
💡 **SUGGESTION: space-joined env lists break label/login names containing spaces**

`ISSUE_LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}` (and `ASSIGNEES` two lines below) are re-split with `.split(' ')` in the probe. GitHub label names may contain spaces (e.g. `status:in progress`), and a label/login token containing a space is silently fractured — `agent:dev` would survive, but any future arming label with a space, or an assignee login, would mismatch. Today this is latent (all five arming labels are space-free), but the parse silently degrades.

Prefer a JSON encoding: `ISSUE_LABELS: ${{ toJson(github.event.issue.labels.*.name) }}` and `JSON.parse(env.ISSUE_LABELS || '[]')` in the probe. Same for assignees.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"

          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi

            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
